title: Waiting in Rotterdam; the Three Dukes and Willie Lewis
summary: While waiting for a Saturday boat, Ramirez sat in at Den Haag with the Three Dukes and met Wilson Myers.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, at that time... I'm getting ahead of my story. We had played... I didn't get to the part where we played
Oh, I didn't realize you went to Denmark, too.
My departure... This has to do with my departure, to get back home. But I can go back further than that, because...
Let's just finish it off. So we go back... I mean, you've got to Rotterdam now. How long did you have to wait there before you caught the boat?
Well, it was.... I don't know. It was about a week. Something like that. Our boat was leaving on a Saturday night at about 11 o'clock.
So you were getting a bit worried.

Well, no, not really, because I knew the boat was in and I had the passes. So in the meantime, Willie Lewis was working at Den Haag in the Tabaris. I went over there. Three buddies of mine were going... I met three buddies of mine, the Three Dukes. One of the Three Dukes was playing piano, because he had no piano player. They asked me if I wanted to stay and play them! [LAUGHS] "No!" It was a great temptation. I said, "Why don't you get Nick(?) (?)?" -- the Dutch pianist. Well, they couldn't get him; I don't know what happened. And the other pianist, Val(?) Hoff(?), he was much too much...I mean, with the Nazis or something; he was very unpopular with the fellow
musicians. Well, I sat in and I played a couple of numbers.
Who were the Three Dukes, then? An act?

An act. Bobby Mosely. Bubba Gaines, who is now with the dancers, the group of dancers now with Honi Coles. Arthur Russell. Those were the Three Dukes. And Wilson Myers came over; we were together. Wilson Myers was playing with Willie Lewis, not as a bass, but as a conga drummer or something. Everybody was trying to get home, you see! He was going, but.... You know, me and Willie had the same passes at the same time.
